- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Underestimate prices during early periods of strong positive sentiment; adjust upward by 3–7% if sentiment > 0.30 in last 3–5 days.
- Lagged forecasts (especially 1–3 day ahead) tend to be too low; add 1–2% to short-term forecasts if sentiment is rising.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–8% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Overshoot after strong positive sentiment: cap forecast at +5% above 14-day moving average if sentiment > 0.40 and price is rising.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (last 5 days < 0.10), reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid sharp upward revisions unless sentiment is >0.40 and price has been trending up for 5+ days.
